# Sweep Decision Inventory

**This is a working artifact for the duration of the prose-and-form-policing sweep, and it is
deleted when the sweep closes.** That is the effort lead's call and it is deliberate: this is a
subtraction pass, and a several-hundred-row ledger that outlives its purpose is exactly the kind of
thing the pass exists to remove. Where a keep row's justification is durable, it belongs at the test
site, not here. Nothing else in the repository should link to this file.

It is step one of the sweep work item in [plan.md](plan.md). It decides nothing else: no deletion
lands with it. The deletions follow as the six PRs the groups below are cut for.

## Basis

Derived at `c686cd6d` (the merge of PR #559), after the wave 1 work that landed before the sweep,
namely PRs #546, #548, #559 and #560. Every `file:line` was read at that commit. Line numbers drift
as the deletion PRs land, so a later reader should treat them as anchors and re-derive, as
[findings.md](findings.md) says of its own.

## How a row was decided

The standard is the always-on `no-prose-policing-tests` rule, as generalized by R1.2 to every
authored artifact, plus [hla.md](hla.md)'s doctrine 2, its source-guard split, and its three-case
`match=` taxonomy. [frd.md](frd.md) R2.2 bounds every row: no row proposes a new production type or
a shipped-contract change, so where preserving an assertion would need a production discriminator,
the row is `delete` and the branch coverage goes with it (R2.4).

- **keep** names the invariant that earns the assertion and what regression it catches. A row that
  could only say "this looks behavioral" was not written; it was read again until it said something.
- **delete** says why nothing real is lost.
- **convert** names the structural replacement and confirms it needs no production change.

Two rules narrowed the keeps more than a shape-based reading would.

**A claim about what an assertion protects was executed, not read.** Four deletions earlier in this
pass were correct while their stated premises were false, each caught only by running. So where a
disposition turned on "some other test already covers this" or "production already enforces this",
the claim was tested. The rows where that changed the answer are called out in the report; they are
not marked in the table, because a row's justification should read the same whether or not it was
the one that surprised us.

**A check is only worth keeping against a guarantee the artifact can hold.** For anything in this
tree, the threat model is accidental regression, never adversarial tampering: whatever can edit the
thing under test can edit the test beside it. That is the correction W1 arrived at after four
rounds, and it is why no row here is justified as proving that nobody can subvert something.

## Groups

The rows are batched by **shape**, not by domain, so each group can land as one PR and a review
round matches the kind of judgment the batch needs. Batching by domain instead would put the
no-judgment mechanical change into the same review as the sweep's riskiest deletions.

| #   | Group                                         | PR shape                                                       |
| --- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Mechanical `match=` narrowing                 | No judgment: the `match=` argument goes, the `raises` stays    |
| 2   | Guide and migration topics                    | The largest single concentration, mostly required-phrase lists |
| 3   | Report lines and hints                        | The judgment-heavy batch                                       |
| 4   | Schema, manifests, capabilities and platforms | Structured-refusal assertions                                  |
| 5   | Authored-artifact form policing               | Config, completions, generated samples, CSS, website           |
| 6   | Source guards                                 | The family `hla.md` settles, decided per guard                 |

## Totals

**1,160 rows: 642 delete, 191 convert, 327 keep.**

The only site count derived exactly is group 1's, because it was scanned mechanically rather than
read: 663 `match=` sites under `cli/tests` and 51 `assertRaisesRegex` sites under `website/tests`,
714 in all. The other groups were read rather than scanned, and one row there covers an assertion
group of one to a dozen lines, so no site total is claimed for them. Do not add these numbers to the
absorbed survey's: that survey counted test FUNCTIONS.

| Group                                            | Rows | delete | convert | keep |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---: | -----: | ------: | ---: |
| 1. Mechanical `match=` narrowing                 |  184 |    171 |       3 |   10 |
| 2. Guide and migration topics                    |   50 |     33 |       3 |   14 |
| 3. Report lines and hints                        |  377 |    224 |      70 |   83 |
| 4. Schema, manifests, capabilities and platforms |  250 |     63 |      85 |  102 |
| 5. Authored-artifact form policing               |  237 |    123 |      19 |   95 |
| 6. Source guards                                 |   62 |     28 |      11 |   23 |

One row is one test or one contiguous assertion group, so a file that mixes wholly-policing tests
with prose assertions riding inside legitimate ones appears several times. Group 1's mechanical
batch is the one exception and says so where it starts: those 155 rows are one per FILE, because 598
sites there share a single shape, a single disposition, and a single justification.

This file is long for the repository's 500-line guidance, deliberately. It is a ledger, it is
temporary, and one row per line is what makes it checkable against a diff.

### The mechanical batch

598 `match=` sites over 155 files, one row per file. Every one is `delete`, and the justification is
shared rather than restated 155 times: no test function in this set raises the same exception type
twice, so the branch under test is selected by its input rather than by the message. Each site is
therefore `hla.md` case 1 (the raised type already discriminates) or case 3 (the sentence is pinned
for its own sake), and both resolve to the same edit. Every matched string is prose this repository
authors, which no case licenses. The `raises` stays; only the `match=` argument goes.

| A-001 | cli/tests/guide/test_migration_topic.py:19-25         | curated cross-topic link + block-type presence                    | convert     | Link resolution is already production-enforced (`guide/catalog.py:133-151` raises `BrokenTopicLinkError` for trusted topics), so the curated-pair restatement is dead weight; the real unguarded invariant is that a topic declaring `related_topics` also carries a `TopicLinks` block. Verified by executing: a contribution with `related_topics` and no `TopicLinks` block parses cleanly and renders with the links silently dropped. Replacement: one catalog-wide check over `build_authored_catalog()` that `topic.related_topics` implies a `TopicLinks` block. No production change.                               |

The lead checked whether the emitted command list could carry it instead and it cannot: convergence is idempotent, so the same chown, chmod and `chmod g+s` run on the fake whether a step changed anything or not, and only the RETURN of each command distinguishes them. The three `*_only_damage` tests exist to pin the owner/mode/sgid OR-collapse against an AND-collapse regression the code comments say was really found; that collapse is an inline `owner.stdout.strip() or mode.stdout.strip() or sgid.stdout.strip()` at `repair.py:189`, not a helper, so unlike `_acls_changed` (B-042) there is nothing to call directly. Extracting one purely so a test could call it is production surface whose only consumer is a test, which `hla.md` doctrine 2 excludes by name. R2.4 therefore resolves it by deletion and the OR-collapse coverage goes with it. |

## Sequencing between the groups

Four constraints bind the order the six PRs land in, beyond the plan's existing ordering against the
`phase7` item, the contained cli items, and P5.

1. **Group 1 lands first, and no other group may lean on it.** A `match=` is a fallback that is
   about to be deleted. Where a row in group 3 or group 4 justified deleting a prose assertion by
   pointing at the `match=` on the same `raises`, that justification expires the moment group 1
   lands. Those rows were re-read and now cite the surviving `raises` type or a structural sibling
   instead. Hold any new row to the same rule.
2. **Group 2 sits downstream of the guide work item.** Several group 2 deletes are justified by
   `cli/tests/guide/test_contract_catalog.py` already enforcing the same rule structurally, and that
   file is on the exclusion list because the guide item owns it. If that item deletes the checks
   these rows lean on, the rows lose their backing.
3. **Group 5 carries the W2 question**, which is an ordering decision rather than something this
   inventory can settle. See the open questions.
4. **Group 3 is too big for one PR at 377 rows.** It is the judgment-heavy batch and the largest by
   a wide margin. The natural cut is by subsystem inside the one shape (consoles and sessions;
   workspaces and agents; vms and platforms; the rest), which keeps the review's judgment uniform
   while making each round reviewable.

## Overlaps found

Per the plan, the sweep records an overlap, keeps the file, and raises the ordering. Ten turned up.

1. **`cli/tests/test_completions.py:163-171` duplicates
   `cli/tests/guide/test_release_notes.py:130-137` line for line**: the same four assertions on the
   dynamic completion snippets, written two ways. Both are in the sweep's scope, so this is an
   ordering note only; the inventory deletes the guide-side copy and leaves the completions-side
   decision with its own row.
2. **`cli/tests/guide/test_contract_catalog.py`** (exclusion list, guide item) is the structural
   home that several group 2 deletes rest on, specifically the block-discriminator closure at
   `:248-250` and the broken-link handling at `:303-319`. Sequencing constraint 2 above.
3. **`cli/tests/secrets/test_resolution_lifecycle.py:542`** is a `format_remediation` pin in the
   same family as S1's `test_resolution_timeout_cleanup.py` wording trims. Different file, so it is
   inventoried here rather than deferred, but the two should be read together.
4. **P5 (gcp fixture extraction)** shares five files with this sweep's gcp rows. The plan already
   orders the sweep first. One fact for whoever runs P5: the E-093 replacement asserts through the
   public `manual_cleanup_guidance`, so it does not touch the per-file `_api_error` or
   extended-operation fakes and rebases cleanly under the extraction.
5. **P4 (gcp's five-class error taxonomy)** is load-bearing for roughly fifteen delete rows that
   rest on "the raised type already discriminates". Nothing in production dispatches on those
   subclasses today, so after this sweep the tests become the taxonomy's only consumer. If the
   reassessment collapses it toward the sibling shape, that branch coverage goes too. Recorded for
   R4.
6. **D2 (deriving `SCHEMA_SENTINELS` by replaying `MIGRATIONS`)** would rewrite
   `cli/tests/test_database_backup.py:61-79`, which this inventory keeps as derivation parity. If D2
   ever runs, that test is its territory.
7. **The CLI grammar rewrite** (saga `phasing.md` puts it directly after wave 1) churns exactly the
   rows that pin the command tree and per-flag help. They are deletes either way, so landing them
   before the rewrite strictly reduces its diff.
8. **`cli/tests/test_ssh_config.py:132-151`** is the unit home of the `"SSH config synced"` line

9. **`cli/tests/capabilities/test_secret_backend_conformance.py`** is the same family as

## Open questions

Consolidated here because a question dropped at the end of a commit message is a question nobody
answers. None of them blocks the deletion PRs; each has a recorded decision that the lead can flip.

1. **The workspace-repair report family is the sweep's largest single deliberate coverage loss**
   (row B-041, seven assertion groups). Decided `delete` under R2.4, and the premise was checked
   rather than assumed: `repair_workspace` returns `None`, convergence is idempotent so the emitted
   command list is identical whether a step changed anything, and the owner/mode/sgid OR-collapse is
   an inline `or` at `repair.py:189` rather than a callable helper. Extracting one so a test could
   call it is production surface whose only consumer is a test. Three whole tests go. Worth the
   lead's eye rather than the lead's trust.
2. **W2 ordering.** 22 of `website/tests/test_site_templates.py`'s 25 tests are delete rows, all of
   them mutate-and-assert-raises against the element-by-element half of `site_validation.py`, which
   is a deferred R4 deletion candidate. The rows are executable now, but landing them leaves roughly
   850 lines of production validator with positive-path coverage only until R4. The principled
   option is to land the block as one unit and say plainly in the PR what it does; the alternative
   is to hold it until W2 is decided.
3. **Does a shipped security header count as an authored artifact?** The website's CSP is asserted
   against a second copy in `site_test_support.CSP`. Recorded as a convert to a directive-level
   check, but it reads three ways and nothing else turns on the answer.
4. **Is a style rule mechanized as a test a "threshold" keep?** `test_site_build.py:273-292` asserts
   the 1,000-line file ceiling that the `code-style` rule states. Recorded as delete because it can
   only fail when someone edits the thing it restates, but doctrine 2 lists thresholds as a keep
   shape.
5. **Does the synthetic-fixture carve-out cover per-row state markers?** Two rows keep rendered
   `(disabled)` / `(not ready)` markers on that basis, and the marker strings are authored.
6. **Formatter-output equality.** The line drawn was: an assertion proving a string propagates
   between two surfaces, or that a rendered line carries registry data, is a keep; an assertion
   fixing the sentence for its own sake is a delete. Six rows move together if the lead draws it
   elsewhere.
7. **Union-collapse cardinality** (`test_spec_workspace_template.py`, eight sites). Several tests
   assert that an env-entry mistake is refused as ONE problem, currently observable only as the
   message's line count. Recorded as delete; if the cardinality is worth keeping, the form is
   `len(str(err).splitlines()) == 1` and it should be decided once for the family.
8. **The one row that proposes adding a test in a subtraction pass** (A-004/A-041). It resolves
   every guide action's command through the real click tree instead of restating the tokens, was
   verified to pass at HEAD and to catch a bogus flag, and needs no production change. It is still
   an addition. Delete-and-record-the-drift-risk is stated in the row as the alternative.
9. **The graph-guard reservation**, recorded in row L-101 rather than acted on. `hla.md` names the
   file as the delete example and the row follows that, but banned pattern 2 reads as a reachability
   rule of the same family as the import-boundary guard the doctrine keeps, and the property is
   genuinely unobservable, since a consumer that re-derives correctly returns the same answer as the
   graph until the two diverge.
10. **Are `agentworks-manual-*` / `agentworks-pre-migration-*` backup filenames a documented
    operator interface?** If they are, one pin is a real contract check rather than a naming
    restatement.
11. **Rows that were reasoned rather than executed** and whose disposition turns on a coverage
    claim: eight in total, each tagged `[unverified]` in its justification. The deletion PR should
    execute them rather than inherit them.

  `capabilities/test_secret_backend_conformance.py` is the same family as `test_conformance.py`,
